No located study directly compares the exact gated recent-item mean residual with all requested controls; its incremental benefit remains unverified. [SASRec](https://arxiv.org/abs/1808.09781) provides the relevant foundation: adaptive history aggregation, with a connection to uniform item aggregation through its FISM reduction. The [official implementation](https://github.com/kang205/SASRec/blob/master/model.py) uses causal attention, padding masks, input embeddings scaled by √d, unscaled tied output embeddings, and final layer normalization. These details should remain consistent across architectural comparisons.

Loss is a major confound. [gSASRec](https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.07192) investigates negative-sampling overconfidence and generalized BCE; [Turning Dross Into Gold Loss](https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.07602) examines SASRec versus BERT4Rec through their differing objectives. Neither establishes the proposed residual’s value, but both motivate crossing architecture variants with loss variants rather than attributing a joint improvement to architecture.

Suggested reproducible experiment, not a published recipe: at every training position t, compute m_t as the padding-masked mean of item embeddings over positions max(1,t−w+1)…t, excluding positional embeddings and future items. Specify raw versus √d-scaled pooling explicitly. Fuse with SASRec state h_t using z_t=h_t+sigmoid(W[h_t;m_t]+b)⊙LN(m_t); initialize W=0, b=−3 for a small initial contribution. Document normalization placement and avoid silently adding another final normalization. Compare standalone last-item and recent-mean models, SASRec alone, last-item residual, fixed-coefficient recent-mean residual, and learned gating. Cross these with original one-negative BCE and the selected multi-negative objective, holding negative draws, tuning budgets, splits, seeds, and validation candidates constant. Select using four-category macro validation HR@10.
